what_happened: Found the real OOM lever: LEAN_NUM_THREADS. Lake has no -j/--jobs flag because Lean exposes no API for a host program to cap its own Task thread pool; the pool size (defaulting to the runner's vCPU count) IS capped via the LEAN_NUM_THREADS env var, confirmed by Lake/Lean maintainers on Zulip, documented in leanprover/lean-action's own README for the structurally identical leanchecker-OOM case, and used in production by opencompl/veir's docs.yml specifically to stop doc-gen4 OOMing ('Lake runs one job per core ... run out of memory'). This is reachable purely as a step-level env var in docs.yml -- no action fork needed.

Dispatch Description asserts docs.yml is unmodified since 2026-09-20; git log -1 on the file gives 477afc84d dated 2026-11-18 (this task's own swap-step commit). Diagnosis unaffected -- the 2026-09-20 figure described the pre-task state -- but the carried figure was stale and is corrected in the plan's Premise Re-Validation section.

The research report named a single decisive lever (LEAN_NUM_THREADS) with two independent production precedents and closed both dispatch-named alternatives by measurement, so planning needed no route adjudication -- only a local falsification probe to close the report's own self-declared Risk 3. Plan authored in two phases with no open user decision.

Phase 1's prescribed probe mechanism (pure Task.spawn) never achieved multi-thread concurrency on this toolchain regardless of LEAN_NUM_THREADS, including at Task.Priority.dedicated; confirmed via /proc thread-state polling on a compiled build. Switched to IO.asTask (the plan's other named mechanism), which did achieve genuine multi-thread concurrency, but the official lake env lean --run measurement still showed no capping effect (1433% CPU unset vs 1669% at LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1), likely because the probe's flat 48-way simultaneous fan-out triggers Lean's documented soft-limit-exceeded-to-avoid-deadlock behavior, a different task shape from Lake's actual dependency-graph-driven job release. Recorded verdict: inconclusive (not confirmed, not refuted), per the plan's own three-way rubric; Phase 2 proceeds per the plan's explicit inconclusive-is-not-a-blocker contingency.
